record.original_question: The function dn(σ, τ) = (1/n)·|{x ∈ {1,..., n} | σ(x) ̸= τ (x)}| is a distance on the symmetric group Sn. For a finitely generated group G, an almost-homomorphism is a sequence of set-theoretic maps fn: G → Sn satisfying dn(fn(g)fn(h), fn(gh)) → 0 as n → ∞ for all g, h ∈ G. An almost-homomorphism {fn } is said to be close to a homomorphism if there is a sequence of group homomorphisms ρn: G → Sn such that dn(ρn(g), fn(g)) → 0 as n → ∞ for all g ∈ G. The group G is said to be permutation stable if every almost-homomorphism of G is close to a homomorphism. Conjecture: Metabelian groups are permutation-stable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, and define the normalized Hamming distance on $S_n$ by
$$d_n(\sigma,\tau) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{n}\,\bigl|\{x \in \{1,\dots,n\} : \sigma(x) \neq \tau(x)\}\bigr|.$$
Let $G$ be a finitely generated group. A sequence of (set-theoretic) maps $f_n : G \to S_n$ is called an almost-homomorphism if
$$d_n\bigl(f_n(g)\,f_n(h),\, f_n(gh)\bigr) \to 0 \quad\text{as } n\to\infty, \text{ for every } g,h\in G.$$
An almost-homomorphism $\{f_n\}$ is said to be close to a homomorphism if there exists a sequence of group homomorphisms $\rho_n : G \to S_n$ with
$$d_n\bigl(\rho_n(g),\, f_n(g)\bigr) \to 0 \quad\text{as } n\to\infty, \text{ for every } g \in G.$$
The group $G$ is called permutation stable if every almost-homomorphism of $G$ is close to a homomorphism.

A group $G$ is metabelian if it admits an abelian normal subgroup $A \trianglelefteq G$ such that $G/A$ is abelian (equivalently, the commutator subgroup $[G,G]$ is abelian).

Prove or disprove: every finitely generated metabelian group is permutation stable.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, attributed to Levit and Lubotzky, remains open in general. Important special cases have been established: Levit–Lubotzky proved permutation stability of permutational wreath products of finitely generated abelian groups; Zheng showed the lamplighter group is permutation stable via co-sofic invariant random subgroups; and a 2023 preprint proves that all finitely generated free metabelian groups are permutation stable. The full conjecture for arbitrary finitely generated metabelian groups has not been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Free metabelian groups are permutation stable
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that all finitely generated free metabelian groups are permutation stable, extending the Levit–Lubotzky method.
status_evidence.claim: Free metabelian groups have been proven permutation stable, but the general metabelian case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Infinitely presented stable groups and invariant random subgroups of metabelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: All IRSs of the lamplighter group are co-sofic, hence the lamplighter group is permutation stable.
status_evidence.claim: Special metabelian groups such as the lamplighter are known to be permutation stable.

status_evidence.title: Uncountably many permutation stable groups
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs uncountably many permutation stable groups, building on Levit–Lubotzky framework for metabelian-type examples.
status_evidence.claim: Active research has produced many permutation-stable examples but not the full metabelian conjecture.
